thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: AUTOMATED PAGE: Canary p95 latency > 1200ms for route /v1/generate on model-redwood-13b (us-west-2-canary). PD incident id: PD1234567

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: incident PD1234567 triggered -> escalated to eng-oncall rotation.

oliver (eng-oncall): Acked on PD. Looking now. Which release is on canary?

maria (SRE): Maria here — this is the v2.4.7 canary (rolled ~12:03 UTC). Deployed by deploy-bot. Canary subset = 3 pods in us-west-2.

chris (infra): Seeing CPU on those pods spike + kernel context switches. Also a rise in p99 memory of the model server. Logs show repeated KV cache misses and this stack:

```
2026-03-15T12:05:11Z ERROR kvcache: missing prefix key for request id=abc123
2026-03-15T12:05:12Z WARN  model-runtime: async_batch_timeout exceeded
2026-03-15T12:05:12Z ERROR transformers: gpuOOM? fallback to CPU path
```

sunita (platform): Interesting — monitoring shows a correlated increase in external embeddings requests hitting the canary (traffic spike from a small customer set). Could be input distribution change exposing a quantization regression.

oliver (eng-oncall): Quick customer-impact check: are any user-facing 5xxs?

maria (SRE): No surge in 5xxs globally. Error rate up from 0.02% -> 0.4% for that route on canary shards only. Latency SLO breaches for customers behind that traffic slice. Ticketing/CS flagged 2 customers experiencing slow responses.

jeremy (product): Those 2 customers are on Dedicated with routing to canary for test traffic — we should notify them about degraded latency ASAP.

dave (ops): I'll open a support banner after we decide mitigation.

oliver (eng-oncall): Mitigation options: 1) divert canary traffic back to stable 2) rollback canary to v2.4.6 3) scale canary nodes 4) apply runtime patch (kvcache TTL tweak). Thoughts?

maria (SRE): Scaling won't fix the workload pattern if it's a regression. Runtime patch is risky without test. Recommend rollback to v2.4.6 for canary set and pause release.

chris (infra): Agreed — logs indicate a change in quantization kernel selection in v2.4.7 that can increase memory working set. Rollback seems safest.

oliver (eng-oncall): OK initiating rollback. I'm running the rollback command and will divert traffic until it's complete.

```
# divert traffic away from canary
kubectl annotate svc model-service traffic-diversion=stable --overwrite
kubectl rollout undo deployment/model-server --to-revision=142 --namespace=prod-us-west-2
```

pagerduty-bot: PD update: PD1234567 assigned to oliver (eng-oncall). Status: acknowledged.

incident-bot: Action log: traffic diversion annotation applied by oliver at 12:11 UTC. Rollback started.

maria (SRE): Rollback pod events: new pods coming up on v2.4.6. Watch for warmup; kv cache warmup will take ~30-90s.

sunita (platform): I'm also toggling automatic model-fallback policy to prefer cpu-quant variant for the affected model while the rollback finishes. Doing: route-policy set model-redwood-13b->cpu-quant for 10m.

chris (infra): Noted. Also increasing alert thresholds temporarily to avoid autopaging on the warmup noise.

oliver (eng-oncall): Rollback completed and all canary pods are now v2.4.6. Observability: p95 dropped from 1.3s -> 420ms within 90s of rollback. No 5xx increase.

incident-bot: PD update: PD1234567 status changed to resolved by oliver at 12:15 UTC.

jeremy (product): Thanks — reaching out to the two affected customers to explain a transient latency blip and that we rolled back the canary. Will follow up with RCA later.

maria (SRE): Quick postmortem notes to capture:
- Trigger: v2.4.7 changed kernel selection for quantized path, increased memory working set for certain embedding-heavy inputs.
- Detection: automated canary p95 alert -> PagerDuty -> oncall.
- Mitigation: traffic diversion + rollback to v2.4.6. Temporary route-policy to cpu-quant variant to reduce risk.
- Customer impact: limited to two customers on canary; no broad outages.

sunita (platform): Follow ups: add a pre-release perf test for extreme input distributions (embedding bursts), add canary heatmap to detect traffic-pattern shifts, and block kernel selection changes without perf flag on by default.

chris (infra): Also adding a safety-net: if p95>800ms on canary for >2min, automatically divert canary traffic and open PD with lower priority so SRE can triage before full page.

oliver (eng-oncall): I'll close PD when product confirms customer outreach. Leaving this thread open for a short time for actions. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

dave (ops): Support banner drafted: "We observed transient latency for a subset of customers during a canary rollout; mitigation applied. We'll share postmortem." Hold until jeremy confirms wording.

jeremy (product): Confirmed. Patch release hold approved for v2.4.7 until SRE signs off.

incident-bot: Incident PD1234567 closed at 12:22 UTC. Log: rollback->stable, customer notif pending.

maria (SRE): Assigning follow-up owners: RCA draft -> maria (SRE), perf test -> sunita (platform), release gating -> chris (infra), customer comms -> jeremy (product). I'll create the follow-up tickets.

oliver (eng-oncall): Good job team. If anything unexpected pops up, ping @oliver.

sunita (platform): minor note: saved a heap dump from one of the canary pods. Will attach to RCA.

chris (infra): putting an entry in the release checklist: "verify quant kernel selection no-op for canary if change isn't flagged".

jeremy (product): Closing loop with CS in 30m.

oliver (eng-oncall): Thread locked for triage until tickets are created. Leaving PD closed but follow-ups open.

incident-bot: Automated summary posted to #incidents and attached to PD1234567.

maria (SRE): I'll post an initial RCA draft in ~1h.

--- end of thread ---
